Implements the Phone-transfer feasibility design, protocol specification v1 and PoC plan.

Phone-transfer transfers data directly between your two phones and never goes through a server by default.

1. Least privilege: a permission is requested only when you select the matching data item; nothing is requested for items you did not select.

2. No data leaves the devices: payloads are protected with AES-256-GCM end-to-end encryption; a packet capture only shows ciphertext.

3. Key lifecycle: session keys live in memory only and are destroyed on timeout, session end or cancellation. They are never written to disk and never backed up.

4. Separate consent: SMS, MMS, call log and app data are L4 critical and require individual consent.

5. Cleanup: temporary caches live in the app private directory and are wiped when the session ends.

6. Redacted logs: only actions and error codes are logged, never content.

7. No hardware identifiers: the session id is random per session; IMEI / serial numbers are never used.

8. Honest limits: iOS apps cannot read SMS, call log, notes or app data. Those items are marked unsupported in the capability map with an alternative path.
